liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Jerry's voice sounds fresh on Iko Iko, but the music is very easygoing and the drums seem absent [19]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O comes across as rather tame [19]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): A skywriter spelled out 'IMPEACH REAGAN' during He's Gone, which stirred up the crowd [15]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The Wheel is nice and relaxed, though low on energy [13]
- **Watching The River Flow** (1 review): Watching The River Flow is singled out as one of the rare songs played at the show [16]
- **Heart Of Mine** (1 review): Heart Of Mine is a rare number, loved for its beautiful, repetitive chord progression [16]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): The Playin' lasts only about five minutes and is mostly unremarkable, a perfunctory showpiece [13]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Stranger is mellow, with Jerry's playing carrying the tune [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-07-19.149779.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 34 songs; 229 min [1]
- **gd1987-07-19.152143.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 35 songs; 227 min [3]
- **gd87-07-19.sbd.fishman.13023.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 144 min; rated 2.8/5 by 10 [6]. Said about its sound: Sound is acceptable but slightly short on bass, with a lot of crowd noise mixed in [13]
- **gd1987-07-19.149748.ultramatrix.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 34 songs; 229 min [2]

## Around the show

- Extremely hot day, reportedly close to the temperature of Veneta in 1972, whose site was near the stadium [15]
- Record rainfall the day before, then a record high-heat day; humid and hot, with portable showers heavily used at the stadium's back [23]
- A California bear figure flew from the stage; the mood was festive and sweaty [23]
- The Dead played in a ho-hum way until Dylan came out, by which time it had started cooling down [23]
- Set 3 and the encore are the Grateful Dead with Bob Dylan, who plays guitar [1]
- Bob Dylan plays guitar in the third set [3]
- Of the three west coast Dylan/Dead shows, this was the most interesting, though Oakland was probably best overall [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-07-19.149779.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 29, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Several sets of masters were combined to complete the Dead's sets; GEMS crew supplied a patch for the show's final 25 seconds [1]
- **gd1987-07-19.152143.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D6 [3]. Also: A ten-second patch in Space comes from Charlie Miller's ultramatrix source [3]
- **gd87-07-19.sbd.fishman.13023.sbeok.shnf**: source: Matrix DSBD>D>CD-R>EAC (0.93) >SHN (MKWACT 97) via JR Fishman [6]
- **gd1987-07-19.149748.ultramatrix.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 29, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Autzen Stadium - July 19, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/july-19-1987) [30]
- Poster by William Smythe Grateful Dead: [1987-07-19 Autzen Stadium, U. of Oregon, Eugene, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-07-19-autzen-stadium-u-of-oregon-eugene-or-usa/) [31]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Press Pass, Bob Dylan/Grateful Dead, Autzen Stadium](https://www.dead.net/archives/1987/clippings/press-pass-bob-dylan-grateful-dead-autzen-stadium) [32]
- Photo by zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 7/19/87 Autzen Stadium, University of Oreg… | Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/2417626747/) [33]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/2417626747/) [34]
